title: Inside Devdutt Padikkal's Technical Reinvention That Powered His Test Comeback
excerpt: India batting coach Sitanshu Kotak praised Padikkal's warm-up century as the culmination of a coaching-driven transformation that turned him from IPL castoff into India's answer at No. 3.
body:
• India batting coach Sitanshu Kotak praised Padikkal's unbeaten 142 in the warm-up match against Sri Lanka Cricket XI ahead of the Galle Test series
  • Padikkal credits technical changes under RCB batting coach Dinesh Karthik and head coach Andy Flower for his resurgence from an IPL 2024 average of 5.42
  • His 2025-26 domestic season produced 725 runs in the Vijay Hazare Trophy at 90.62 average and 543 runs in the Ranji Trophy at 60.33
  • With Sai Sudharsan ruled out due to injury, Padikkal is set for his first Test appearance in 20 months at Galle

India batting coach Sitanshu Kotak singled out Devdutt Padikkal's unbeaten 142 in the warm-up match against Sri Lanka Cricket XI as a standout performance ahead of the first Test at Galle. But that innings was the culmination of a technical overhaul that began in an RCB training facility, where Padikkal reworked the foundations of his batting.

From Rock Bottom to Red-Ball Dominance

Just two years ago, Padikkal was in crisis. During IPL 2024 with Lucknow Super Giants, the left-hander averaged 5.42 with a strike rate of 71.69 across seven matches, according to ESPN. He couldn't hit a single six and managed just three fours off 53 balls. LSG released him before the mega auction.

https://x.com/CricCrazyJohns/status/2088581459292668007

Royal Challengers Bengaluru bought him for INR 2 crore, reuniting Padikkal with a franchise he had represented in his first two IPL seasons. What followed was a deliberate, ground-up rebuild under the guidance of RCB batting coach Dinesh Karthik and head coach Andy Flower.

"Technically, there were a few things I needed to change in order to be at my best. DK and Andy have worked on me relentlessly over the last couple of months, and that's really working now."

— Devdutt Padikkal, speaking to ESPN

The Technical Shift

Former India cricketer R Ashwin, who played alongside Padikkal at Rajasthan Royals, identified the specific changes on his YouTube channel. "He was there with me in RR, and at the time, he used to play spinners on the back foot. Now, he plays the reverse sweep and sweep. He also has the feet usage," Ashwin said.

The improvements were measurable. In IPL 2026, Padikkal's strike rate against spin jumped to 152.5 from 131.6 the previous season, according to Yardbarker. His overall strike rate of 173.10 reflected a batter playing with new intent and an expanded shot selection. He finished with 464 runs in 16 matches at a strike rate of 168.72, helping RCB win a second consecutive title, according to Wisden.

The transformation carried into domestic cricket with even greater force. In the 2025-26 Vijay Hazare Trophy, Padikkal scored 725 runs at an elite average of 90.62, hitting four centuries in five matches at one stage, per Wisden. In the Ranji Trophy, he made 543 runs at 60.33, highlighted by a career-best 232 in the semi-final against Uttarakhand. In the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy, he added 309 runs at a strike rate of 167.02, according to Cricinfo.

Kotak's Assessment

The warm-up match against Sri Lanka Cricket XI gave Padikkal a chance to showcase his readiness in match conditions. Batting at No. 3 after Yashasvi Jaiswal fell for a second-ball duck, Padikkal walked in at 0 for 1 and proceeded to dismantle the opposition attack. His 142 not out featured 18 boundaries in what Cricinfo described as "a clinic in technical discipline and intent."

"I think Devdutt batted really well. For me, Devdutt's innings was really good," Kotak told bcci.tv, according to Cricket Country. He emphasized the value of match practice over net sessions: "Practicing in nets for four more days won't be as productive as playing the practice match."

A Door That Opened at the Right Time

Padikkal's path to the Test XI cleared when incumbent No. 3 Sai Sudharsan was ruled out of the Sri Lanka series due to a toe injury sustained during India A's tour. According to Cricinfo, head coach Gautam Gambhir has a tactical preference for a left-handed presence in the top order, and Padikkal's ability to use his long stride against spin makes him suited for Galle's conditions — something he demonstrated during India A's tour of Sri Lanka, where he scored a 94 in the second unofficial Test.

Padikkal has played just two Tests for India: a debut 65 against England in Dharamsala in 2024 and a tougher outing in Perth later that year. The Galle Test represents his first appearance in 20 months — and few players have arrived at such an opportunity better prepared.

As Ashwin put it: "I want Devdutt Padikkal to be India's No. 3 in Test cricket. He has batted so well, and he deserves to be an incumbent Test player for India. He should be given a long-term chance."
nri_angle: Padikkal's resurgence under coaching mentorship highlights the depth of Indian cricket talent development and the role of IPL coaching structures.
